overall_summary: Bitcoin faces clear near-term pressure after Binance’s record $6.3 billion hack and over $1.5 billion in long liquidations, with stolen coins already split into hard-to-freeze wallets. ETF inflows and Strategy’s continued buying offer support, yet Iran-Hormuz tensions and sticky inflation keep risk appetite capped. Overall tone stays defensive despite a softer dollar.
key_points: Record Binance hack dominates crypto sentiment
Heavy long liquidations amplify selling pressure
Spot ETF inflows remain a key offset
Hormuz tanker hits raise geopolitical risk
Weaker DXY gives only limited relief

items.title: Binance Suffers Record $6.3B Hack, Largest in Crypto History
items.summary: Hackers drained roughly six point three billion dollars from Binance hot wallets across multiple chains in about twenty minutes late Thursday, with investigators linking it to North Korean groups. Binance paused deposits and withdrawals, estimated the impact at six point three billion, said about three billion has been frozen so far, and pledged to cover all user losses from its SAFU fund and company resources. Bitcoin slid below seventy-seven thousand and briefly toward seventy-six thousand on the news. Traders should care because this is a major confidence shock for the biggest exchange and can keep risk appetite suppressed until withdrawals resume and more funds are recovered.
items.impact: Near-term selling pressure and exchange-risk premium on BTC and alts

items.title: Crypto Liquidations Hit $1.5B-Plus as Longs Get Wiped
items.summary: The Binance-driven selloff forced more than one point five billion dollars in crypto futures liquidations over twenty-four hours, with longs making up roughly eighty-four percent of the total. Bitcoin and ether accounted for the bulk, and Binance itself handled nearly half the liquidations. Price briefly tagged the mid-seventy-six thousands before a partial bounce. Traders should care because the cascade amplified the drop and flushed leverage, which can set up either a cleaner base or further volatility if support fails.
items.impact: Forced selling cascade that deepens short-term downside

items.title: Hacker Splits 18,270 Stolen BTC Into 19 Unfreezable Wallets
items.summary: About eighteen thousand two hundred seventy bitcoin worth roughly one point four billion dollars taken in the Binance breach were quickly split across nineteen wallets, seventeen of them holding exactly one thousand BTC each. None of those coins had moved as of early Friday, and unlike stablecoins they cannot be frozen by issuers. This leaves a large unrecoverable chunk still under attacker control. Traders should watch for any movement that could signal dumping or further laundering pressure on the market.
items.impact: Persistent overhang risk from movable stolen BTC

items.title: US Spot Bitcoin ETFs Add Over $420M Across Three Sessions
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net inflows of about one hundred thirty-seven million on Wednesday and continued positive on Thursday with roughly seventeen million, bringing three-day additions above four hundred twenty-three million dollars, led by BlackRock’s IBIT. Total net assets sit near one hundred four billion. This shows institutional spot demand holding up even as the market digested the Binance shock. Traders should care because sustained ETF buying can offset exchange-driven fear and provide a bid under price.
items.impact: Supportive institutional demand cushioning the selloff

items.title: Strategy Posts Record $21B Q3 Income, Eyes More BTC Buys
items.summary: Strategy reported record operating income of about twenty-one billion dollars in the third quarter, almost entirely from mark-to-market gains on its bitcoin, and net income near nineteen point five billion. Holdings stood at roughly eight hundred forty-eight thousand five hundred BTC. On the earnings call Michael Saylor said the balance sheet could support up to thirty billion in digital credit for further purchases without new common equity or higher BTC prices, while management signaled more buying via preferreds. Traders should care because the largest corporate holder is still aggressively accumulating and framing a new bull phase.
items.impact: Reinforces corporate treasury demand narrative for BTC

items.title: Tether, Circle Freeze Billions in Stolen Stablecoins
items.summary: Stablecoin issuers moved fast after the Binance breach, with Tether freezing nearly one point five seven billion in USDT and Circle more than eight hundred million in USDC, contributing to roughly two point seven to three billion total frozen across partners. Binance said it is working with issuers and chain analytics firms and expects to resume withdrawals within about forty-five hours. This containment limits how much of the haul can immediately hit open markets. Traders should care because successful freezes reduce the immediate sellable supply overhang and support the exchange’s ability to make users whole.
items.impact: Partial damage control that may aid stabilization once withdrawals reopen

items.title: Fed Holds Rates at 3.75-4% With Two Hawkish Dissents
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept the funds rate unchanged in a 10-2 vote on Wednesday, with Governors Cook and Hammack preferring a quarter-point hike. The statement called growth strong, productivity robust, and inflation still elevated, stressing that more data will guide the next move toward the two percent goal. Chair Warsh's press conference avoided locking in a December hike. Traders should care because December hike odds remain high and the pause leaves markets data-dependent heading into midterms and more inflation prints.
items.impact: Keeps higher-for-longer rates in play; mixed for risk assets pending data

items.title: Q3 GDP Beats at 3.4% on Spending and AI Investment
items.summary: Advance third-quarter GDP rose at a 3.4 percent annualized pace, beating the 3.2 percent forecast and accelerating from 2.2 percent. Consumer spending held firm at about 3.8 percent while business investment, especially in AI, surged. The strong print came one day after the Fed held rates and described the economy as expanding robustly. Crypto traders should watch this because solid growth supports risk appetite even as it reduces odds of near-term easing.
items.impact: Supports risk-on sentiment and equity/crypto resilience short-term

items.title: September Core PCE Hits 3.1% as Expected, Still Elevated
items.summary: Core PCE rose 0.3 percent month-over-month and 3.1 percent year-over-year, matching forecasts and edging up from prior readings. Headline PCE came in at 0.5 percent monthly and 3.6 percent annually, driven partly by energy. Personal spending slowed to 0.5 percent while income rose just 0.2 percent. This is the Fed's preferred gauge, so the still-high level keeps December rate-hike probability elevated and pressures longer-term yields.
items.impact: Reinforces higher-for-longer Fed path, potential headwind for Bitcoin

items.title: BoJ Holds at 1.25%, Declares 2% Inflation Target Met
items.summary: The Bank of Japan left its policy rate unchanged at 1.25 percent in an 8-1 vote on Friday, with one member wanting a hike. It said underlying inflation is now generally consistent with the two percent target for the first time since 2013 and raised its 2027 inflation forecasts. The bank also accelerated ETF sales. This hawkish hold could support the yen and signal further global tightening pressure.
items.impact: Yen support and global rate signals; limited immediate crypto direction

items.title: ECB Holds Rates; Lagarde to Step Down Early in February
items.summary: The European Central Bank kept its deposit rate at 2.50 percent on Thursday in a hawkish hold, citing rising energy prices as upside inflation risks. President Christine Lagarde announced she will leave early on February 7 2027 to gain freedom to speak on non-monetary issues. The succession race begins amid French fiscal concerns. Euro-area policy uncertainty and energy-driven inflation remain key for global dollar and risk flows.
items.impact: Euro volatility and policy uncertainty; secondary for US crypto markets

items.title: DXY Slides Toward 101.6 as Yields Ease Post-Data
items.summary: The US dollar index extended losses toward the 101.60-101.70 area on Friday, down for a third session, while the 10-year Treasury yield slipped near 4.93 percent. Softness followed the Fed hold, mixed tech earnings jitters, and the GDP-PCE package. Jobless claims stayed low at 194k. A weaker dollar often lifts crypto, but elevated rate expectations and strong growth keep the backdrop mixed.
items.impact: Weaker DXY typically supportive for Bitcoin and risk assets

items.title: CENTCOM Chief Briefs Trump on Iran Strike Options
items.summary: The top U.S. commander in the Middle East, Admiral Brad Cooper, made a rare in-person White House visit Thursday to brief President Trump on military options against Iran. Defense Secretary Hegseth and the Joint Chiefs chairman joined as the administration weighs a short intense campaign after next week's midterms. Gulf allies have already been told to prepare. Traders should care because any green light keeps the oil risk premium elevated and fuels risk-off moves across equities and crypto.
items.impact: Heightened escalation risk supports oil and pressures risk assets

items.title: Vance Sends Letter to Iranian Hardliner for Peace Talks
items.summary: Vice President JD Vance contacted Iran's Supreme National Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei via Qatari mediators in a bid to restart direct negotiations. The outreach, approved by Trump, seeks a framework that could include nuclear issues and reopening the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for sanctions relief. Iran is drafting a reply while hardline conditions remain. This is the key swing factor for markets: successful talks would crush the oil premium and spark a risk-on rally, while failure clears the path for post-election strikes.
items.impact: Unresolved diplomacy leaves oil and risk assets range-bound pending Iran reply

items.title: Iran Claims Multiple Tankers Hit Mines in Hormuz
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said four oil tankers caught fire after striking mines while using unauthorized routes through the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC also reported intercepting a U.S. drone and warding off a hostile fighter jet near Qeshm Island. Maritime agencies confirmed at least one vessel on fire. This keeps global oil supply fears alive even as some flows recover, directly feeding higher energy prices that squeeze growth and risk appetite.
items.impact: Sustains oil risk premium and weigh on risk assets including Bitcoin

items.title: Israel Election Deadlock: Neither Bloc Wins Majority
items.summary: Final vote counts confirmed Netanyahu's right-wing bloc at 53 seats and the main opposition at 48 in the 120-seat Knesset, with Arab parties holding 19 as potential kingmakers. Neither side can form a government alone, triggering coalition talks and investigations into vote-stealing claims. Political paralysis in Israel during the Iran conflict adds uncertainty for U.S. regional strategy and could delay decisive action or complicate alliances.
items.impact: Adds political uncertainty premium without immediate directional catalyst

items.title: Ukraine Pauses Strikes on Russian Oil Refineries
items.summary: Ukraine's military has unofficially halted long-range drone attacks on Russian oil refineries after sustained pressure from President Trump, who blames the strikes for high diesel prices. The pause began mid-October and is expected to last at least through the U.S. midterms. Russia continues hitting Ukrainian energy targets. This could temporarily ease some refined product tightness and support Trump's diesel import deal narrative, offering modest relief to energy-driven inflation fears.
items.impact: Potential short-term cooling in diesel prices supports risk appetite

items.title: Russian Drone Strike Kills 13 at Dnipro Train Station
items.summary: A Russian drone slammed into a crowded train platform in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro, killing at least 13 people and wounding more. This comes as Russia steps up attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure while Ukraine holds fire on Russian refineries. The ongoing war and civilian toll keep European energy and security risks in focus ahead of G20 talks, limiting any broad risk-on move until clearer de-escalation signals appear.
items.impact: Reinforces Ukraine war risk and energy infrastructure vulnerability
